questions.question_text: A solution is made up of alcohol and water in an unknown ratio. If one-fourth of this solution is taken out and replaced with water, the ratio is reversed. What is the volume of water(in liters) in the final solution if the volume of the solution is 35 liters?
questions.solution_text:
Consider total volume of solution = L and the ratio of alcohol and water is a:b
Volume of alcohol = aL/(a+b)    Volume of water = bL/(a+b) 
After taking out L/4 solution, the ratio will remain same.
Volume of alcohol = 3aL/4(a+b)    Volume of water = 3bL/4(a+b) 
After adding L/4 water, Volume of alcohol = 3aL/4(a+b)    Volume of water = 3bL/4(a+b) + L/4
New ratio of volume of alcohol to water = $\frac{\frac{3aL}{4(a+b)}}{\frac{3bL}{4(a+b)}+\frac{L}{4}}$ = $\frac{b}{a}$
$\frac{3a}{3b+a+b} = \frac{b}{a}$
$\frac{3a}{4b+a} = \frac{b}{a}$
$3a^{2} = 4b^{2}+ab$   $3a^{2} -ab-4b^{2}= 0$     $3a^{2} +3ab-4ab-4b^{2}= 0$
$(a+b)(3a-4b)=0$   $\frac{a}{b}$ = 4/3    (If (a+b)=0, one value is negative, ignore negative value)
Since in final solution ratio becomes 3:4, volume of water = 35*(4/7) = 20 liters
C is the answer.

questions.question_text: The sum of lengths of the parallel sides of a trapezium is 30 cm. The lengths of parallel sides are in the ratio 3:7. One of the non-parallel sides is perpendicular to the other two sides. If the area of the trapezium is 135 $cm^2$, find perimeter of the trapezium.
questions.solution_text:
Let us look at a diagram of the situation. 
Let the lengths of the parallel sides be $3x$ and $7x$. 
Since we know that the sum of lengths of the parallel sides is 30 cm, 
$3x+7x = 30 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{30}{10} \Rightarrow x =3$
Thus the lengths of the sides are 9 cm and 21 cm respectively.
Let the given figure be the figure of the trapezium : 
Here, AB=9 cm and CD=21 cm.
Let us draw a perpendicular from C on BD meeting BD at point E. 
Here, ABCE is a square with side 9 cm. Therefore, $\triangle BED$ is a right angled triangle. 
Let the length of ED be $y$ cm. 
Then area of $\triangle BED, A' = \dfrac{1}{2} \times BE \times ED $
$ \Rightarrow A' = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 \times y $
Since the area of the trapezium is given, 
Area of trapezium = Area of square + Area of triangle 
$\Rightarrow 135 = (9 \times 9)+(\dfrac{9y}{2}) $
$\Rightarrow 15 = 9+ \dfrac{y}{2} \Rightarrow y = 2 \times 6 = 12 $
Applying pythagoras theorem on $\triangle BED$, $12^2+9^2 = BD^2 $
$ \Rightarrow BD^2 = 225 \Rightarrow BD = 15 $cm 
Thus, perimeter of the trapezium = 9+21+9+15 = 54 cm

questions.question_text: Two racers are running to and fro from points A and B at 3m/s and 7m/s respectively. If the distance between A and B is 2000m, what is the total distance covered by both the racers, till they meet for the 2nd time?
questions.solution_text:
Two racers are running from point A and B respectively at 3m/s and 7m/s.
The racers will meet for the first time at $2000\times\ \frac{3}{10}=600m$ from A.
Now they will move in the direction opposite to each other till the racer from B reach A, after that, both racers will move in the same direction.
When the faster racer reaches A, then the slower racer will cover x km till then
Thus, 
$\frac{x}{3}=\frac{2000}{7}$    (Equating time taken)
x= $\frac{6000}{7}$
The relative speed at that point of time = 7-3=4m/s
After reaching A, the time taken by the faster racer to catch the slower racer = $\frac{6000}{7\times4}$
Distance travelled by the faster racer from A till he meets the slower racer for the second time =7 * $\frac{1500}{7}$=1500m
This distance will also be equal to the total distance travelled by the slower racer(from the figure) = 1500m
The distance travelled by the faster racer = Distance from B to A + 1500 = 2000+1500 m
Total distance travelled= 1500+(2000+1500)=5000m

questions.question_text: There are two alcohol solutions A and B such that A is a 43% alcohol solution and B has 53 parts alcohol for every 47 parts water. If we mix the two solutions to get another alcohol solution, that has at least 50% alcohol, which of the following can be the ratios in which the A and B can be mixed?
questions.solution_text:
By the concept of alligations, we can say that to get a 50% solution, we need A and B in the ratio of 
(53-50):(50-43) = 3:7
Now if we increase the proportion of A, then it will bring the final concentration to less than 50%, but if we increase B, we get a value more than the required fifty percentage alcohol solution; hence, we can have a ratio less than 3:7 but not more than it. Hence, option c is right.
Alternate Explanation: 
The ratio of alcohol percentage and water percentage in A and B are $43:53$ and $57:47$, respectively.
Now let the solutions be mixed in the ratio $X:Y$.
Since alcohol content should be more than 50%, the alcohol content will be more than the water content.
Or $43X\ +53Y\ \ge 57X\ +\ 47Y$
Or $\frac{X}{Y} \le \frac{3}{7}$
Or $\frac{X}{Y} \le 0.428$
Only option C has a ratio of X and Y less than or equal to 0.42.
Thus, the correct option is C.

questions.question_text: From a wholesaler, the shopkeeper bought 4 items P, Q, R and S at price of p, q, r and s respectively. He sells the four items at profit of 15%, 25%, 35% and 45% respectively. The net profit on the sale of these four items is 40%. Which of the following options cannot be the value of the ratio p : q : r : s?
questions.solution_text:
Cost price of the items P, Q, R and S are p, q, r and s respectively
Selling price of the items will be 1.15p, 1.25q, 1.35r, 1.45s. 
Profits on individual items will be 0.15p, 0.25q, 0.35r, 0.45s
Further since the net profit is 40% we have, 
$\frac{0.15p + 0.25q + 0.35r + 0.45s}{p + q + r + s} = 0.4$
0.15p + 0.25q + 0.35r + 0.45s = 0.4p + 0.4q + 0.4r + 0.4s
0.05s = 0.05r + 0.15q + 0.25p
s = r + 3q + 5p
All options except D satisfy the equation. 
Hence, option D is the right choice.

questions.question_text: In a test, there are 100 questions. Each question that is correctly answered fetches +3 and a question that is wrongly answered fetches -2. Every question needs to be attempted. If the passing score is 40% of the maximum possible score in the test, how many questions need to be correct to get a score that is double the passing score?
questions.solution_text:
Total possible score is 100 x 3 = 300
New passing score = 2 x 40% of 300 = 240
Now we can assign +3 to all questions and then subtract (+3 + 2) for each incorrect question.
Hence, if the number of incorrect questions is x,
300 - 5x = 240
5x = 60
x = 12
Hence, the number of correct questions = 100 - 12 = 88.

questions.question_text: A system of four spheres of 11 cm radius is stacked to form a pyramid on a wooden floor, such that three sphere are touching the floor and every sphere touches all other spheres. Which of the following is closest to the distance from the topmost point to the base of this system?
questions.solution_text:
We can form a pyramid by stacking one sphere on a base of three spheres. The centres of the spheres forming the bottom layer are 'r' cms above the wooden floor. On connecting the centres of the spheres, we obtain a tetrahedron as shown below: 
Calculating 'h'  from the above setup and adding it to twice the radius of the sphere will render us our desired answer. 
Since AP bisects the equilateral triangle forming the base, $\angle\ PAB\ =\ 30^{\circ\ }$
$a\cos\ 30^{\circ}=r\ ;\ \therefore\ a\ =\frac{2r}{\sqrt{3}\ }$
We can find h in terms of 'r' by using the Pythagoras theorem: $h^2+a^2=4r^2$
On solving we obtain, $h=2r\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$
Hence, the total height till the top of the sphere would be (h + r + r) = $2r\left(1+\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\right)$ $\approx\ 40\ cms$
Thus, Option A is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum value that the function $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2+3x-6}{x^2+3x+6} $ ?
questions.solution_text:
We can simplify the given expression as follows : 
$f(x) =\dfrac{x^2+3x-6}{x^2+3x+6} $
$\Rightarrow f(x) =\dfrac{x^2+3x+6-12}{x^2+3x+6} $
$\Rightarrow f(x) =1 - \dfrac{12}{x^2+3x+6} $ ------(1)
We can see that the value of function f(x) will be minimum when the value of expression $\dfrac{12}{x^2+3x+6}$ is maximum. The value of expression $\dfrac{12}{x^2+3x+6}$ will be maximum when the value of $x^2+3x+6$ is minimum. 
Let, U(x) = $x^2+3x+6$. We know that U(x) will be minimum at x = -b/2a and then minimum value will be equivalent to -D/4a. {Where D is the discriminant and 'a' is the coefficient of $x^2$}
Therefore, U(x)$_{min}$ = $\dfrac{-(3^2-4*1*6)}{4*1}$ = $\dfrac{15}{4}$.
Hence, f(x)$_{min}$ = $1-\dfrac{12}{\frac{15}{4}}$ = $\dfrac{-11}{5}$. Therefore, option C is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: If $2<a<4$ and [a] = The greatest integer less than a, What is the probability (p) of $[a^{2}] = [a]^2$?
questions.solution_text:
Given function is $[a^{2}] = [a]^2$
Let us consider RHS
If $[a]^2$ = 4
then $2 \leq a<3$
If $[a]^2$ = 9
Then $3 \leq a<4$
Let us consider LHS
If $[a^{2}] = 4$
Then $2<a \leq \sqrt{5}$
If $[a^{2}] = 9$ 
Then $3\leq a < \sqrt{10}$ 
Hence, the range satisfying $[a^{2}] = [a]^2$ is $(2, \sqrt{5})$ and $[3,\sqrt{10})$
Required probability = $\frac{\sqrt{5}-2 +\sqrt{10}-3}{4-2}$ = $\frac{2.23-2+3.16-3}{2}$ = $\frac{0.39}{2}$ ~0.2
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: How many straight lines can be drawn with 15 points on a plane of which 7 are collinear?
questions.solution_text:
If we select any 2 points, we can draw a straight line.
So, total number of straight lines = $15_{C_2}$
But, we cannot draw $7_{C_2}$ lines using the 7 collinear points, we can draw only one.
So, we'll subtract those cases from the total number of cases.
Finally, number of straight line that can be drawn = $^{15}C_2\ -\ ^7C_2+1$ = 85

questions.question_text: Pawan and Rushit decide to run on a circular track from the same point in the same direction. The length of the track is 2 km. Ramesh, a bystander, notices that when they (Pawan and Rushit) first meet, Pawan is already in his fourth round and has completed 500 m. How much head start should Pawan give Rushit if he wants a race of 2340 meters  (on a linear track) to end in a draw? (Speed of Pawan is greater than that of Rushit)
questions.solution_text:
When they first met, Pawan had completed 3 + 500/2000 = 3.25 laps.
In this time, Rushit would have completed 1 less round than Pawan.
Thus, Rushit would have completed 2.25 laps.

questions.question_text:
Find the range of ‘x’ for which the following inequality holds true.
$\frac{x^2 - 15}{x^2 + 5} \geq \frac{2x^2 - 16}{x^4 + 5x^2}$
questions.solution_text:
$\frac{x^2 - 15}{x^2 + 5} \geq \frac{2x - 16}{x^4 + 5x^2}$
=> $\frac{x^2 - 15}{x^2 + 5} \geq \frac{2x - 16}{x^2(x^2 + 5)}$
=> $x^2*(x^2 - 15) \geq 2x^2 - 16$
Replacing $x^2$ with t, we get
=> $ t*(t - 15) \geq 2t - 16$
=> $t^2 - 15t \geq 2t - 16$
=> $t^2 - 17t - 16 \geq 0 $
=> $(t - 16)(t - 1) \geq 0$
=> $ t \geq 16$ or $t \leq 1$
=> $ x^2 \geq 16$ or $x^2 \leq 1$
=> $ x \geq 4$ $\cup$ $ x \leq -4$ $\cup$ $ -1 \leq x \leq 1 $ - {0}
x cannot be 0 as in that case the denominator of the RHS would be 0.

questions.question_text: 2 cards are drawn from a deck of 52 cards. What is the probability that both of them are from the same suit?
questions.solution_text:
Total number of ways of selecting two cards = 52C2
In a pack of cards, there are 4 suits and each suit has 13 cards each.
So for 2 cards to be from the same suit, we can select any suit in 4c1 ways and then 2 cards can be selected in 13c2 ways.
Hence the required probability is $\frac{4C1*13C2}{52C2} = 12/51$

questions.question_text: In a geometric progression, the sum of the first 8 terms is equal to the sum of the first 10 terms. The third term of the series is 4. The sum of the first 99 terms of the series is
questions.solution_text:
Let the first term in the series be 'a' and the common ratio be 'r'
Sum of the first 8 terms = Sum of the first 10 terms
$a+ar+ar^2$.......$ar^7$ = $a+ar+ar^2$.........$ar^7+ar^8+ar^9$
$ar^8$ + $ar^9$ = 0
$ar^8\left(r+1\right)=0$
r+1 = 0
r = -1
The series will be 4, -4, 4, -4.....
So nth term will be 4 if n is odd or it will be -4 if n is even.
So 99th term in the series = 4
The sum of the first 98 terms of the series will be 0.
Hence, the sum of the first 99 terms of the series is 4

questions.question_text: The smallest altitude of a right-angled triangle of area 216 cm$^2$ is 14.4 cm. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
questions.solution_text:
We know that the length of an altitude in a triangle is inversely proportional to the length of the side on which it is drawn.
So, the smallest altitude in a right-angled triangle must be drawn on its hypotenuse.
Let the base of the triangle be '$b$', perpendicular be '$p$' and the hypotenuse be '$h$'
Area of the triangle = 216 cm$^2$
or, $\dfrac{1}{2} * b * p = 216$
or, $bp = 432$..........(i)
Also, the length of the altitude drawn on the hypotenuse is 14.4 cm
So, area of the triangle can be written as
$\dfrac{1}{2} * h * 14.4 = 216$
=> $h = 30$ cm
We also know that in a right angled triangle
$b^2 + p^2 = h^2$ [Pythagoras Theorem]
or, $b^2 + p^2 = 30^2 = 900$
Adding '$2bp$' to both the sides, we get
$b^2 + p^2 + 2bp = 900 + 2bp$
Putting the value of $bp$ from (i), we get
$(b + p)^2 = 900 + 2*432 = 1764$
or, $(b + p) = \sqrt{1764} = 42$
Thus, the perimeter of the triangle = $(b + p + h) = (42 + 30) = 72$cm
Hence, option C is the correct answer.

After changing the ratio, the new cost price = $\frac{2a+3b}{5}$
The new selling price per kg = $\frac{2a+3b}{5}\times\ \left(1+\frac{20}{100}\right)$ = $\frac{6\left(2a+3b\right)}{25}$
Since both the selling prices are the same. $\frac{3a+2b}{4}=\frac{6\left(2a+3b\right)}{25}$
=> 25(3a+2b)=24(2a+3b)
=> 75a-48a = 72b-50b
=> 27a = 22b
=> $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{22}{27}$ .....(1)
Cost price per kg while mixing in the ratio 1:4 = $\frac{a+4b}{5}$ = 
Selling price per kg = $\frac{3a+2b}{4}$
% Profit = $\left(\dfrac{SP}{CP}-1\right)\times\ 100=\left(\dfrac{\left(3a+2b\right)\times\ 5}{4\times\ \left(a+4b\right)}-1\right)\times\ 100$
$=\ \left(\dfrac{\ 15a+10b}{4a+16b}-1\right)\times\ 100\ =\ \dfrac{\frac{11a}{b}-6}{\frac{4a}{b}+16}\times\ 100\ $

questions.question_text: A family consisted of four members. In the year 2008, a 60 years old person dies and the average age of the family decreased by 8. Then in the year 2012, a baby is born. In which year the average age of the family will again be equal to the original average age of the family just before the person had died.
questions.solution_text:
Assume the average age before the person dies = a
Then the sum of ages = 4a
After the person dies, the average = $\frac{\left(4a-60\right)}{3}=a-8$
=> a = 36
So, the new average = 36-8 = 28
In the year 2012, the age of each person will increase by 4, hence the average will also increase by 4.
Before the baby is born, the average = 28+4 = 32
=> the sum of ages = 32*3 = 96
After the baby is born, the sum of ages will remain the same, but the number of members will increase to 4.
Hence, the new average = $\frac{96}{4}=24$
It will take 12 years for the average to become 24+12 = 36
Hence the year will be 2012+12 = 2024.

questions.question_text: A group of workers can complete a piece of work in a certain number of days. The entire group starts doing the work but however after 18 days one-fourth of the workers left. To complete the remaining work the remaining group took as much time as the entire group would have taken to complete the whole work. What is the total time that would have been taken to complete the entire work, if instead, one-third of the group had left after working for 24 days?
questions.solution_text:
Let us suppose that ‘x’ men can do the complete work in ‘y’ days. 
It is given that the whole group worked for 18 days and three-fourth of the group worked for the remaining days and completed the work in as much time as the entire group would have taken to complete the whole work.
So we get,
$xy=18x+\frac{3}{4}xy$
$y=72$ days
Now we need to find the time that would have been taken to complete the entire work, if instead, one-third of the group had left after working for 24 days.
Let that time be ‘z’ days
So we get,
$xy=24x+\frac{2}{3}xz$
$72x-24x=\frac{2}{3}xz$
$z=72$ days
Hence, the total number of days = 72 + 24 = 96 days
Hence Option C.
